label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article I, Section 9, Clause 7. No money may be drawn from the Treasury except by appropriations made by law, and a regular statement and account of the receipts and expenditures of all public money must be published from time to time. It reads: “No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law; and a regular Statement and Account of the Receipts and Expenditures of all public Money shall be published from time to time.”
This story is about who decides when money may leave the public funds.

In Federalist 58 (February 1788) Madison wrote that the House of Representatives can not only refuse but alone propose the supplies for government, so "They, in a word, hold the purse," the instrument by which, in British constitutional history, an "infant and humble representation of the people" gradually enlarged "the sphere of its activity and importance."
The deal gives Israel nearly $4 billion each year until September 2028.
The strongest argument against this is that this clause only stops taking money out, so ending aid takes nothing and can be done alone.
We read this clause to mean no money leaves unless a law allows it.
A deal to stop the aid, which Trump says he made with Netanyahu, would not replace that rule.
This keeps the power over spending with the people's lawmakers.
